harry: PR #5950 - unify pagination snippets across py/ts/go. Main asks: show resume-token checkpointing, small retry helper, and note TTL. https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-docs/pull/5950

priya: looks useful. quick check: do we want the Go example to use channels or iterator-style? channels are more idiomatic for streaming pages.

aj: channels + helper is my plan. I'll add a small `ResumeToken` struct, `IsExpired()` helper, and a `SaveCheckpoint(file)` example. For TS Ill export `retryWithBackoff` util. For Py: async iterator + sync wrapper.

docs-bot: snippet-harness/5950 started

lee: CI flagged a broken import in ts: examples/pagination/ts/retry.ts -> should be `import { backoff } from '../../utils/backoff'` not '../../util'

aj: pushing fix now. also adding comment in each snippet: `// tokens expire ~15m by default`

harry: nice. add a one-line changelog entry explaining resumed pagination behavior and TTL assumption.

docs-bot: snippet-harness/5950 failed (go): examples/pagination/go/checkpoint.go:18: undefined: ResumeToken

aj: repro - I renamed the type locally. pushing patch to restore `ResumeToken` name.

aj: (pushed) short go snippet:
```go
// checkpoint.go
package pagination

type ResumeToken struct {
  Cursor string `json:\"cursor\"`
  ExpiresAt int64 `json:\"expires_at_unix\"`
}

func (t *ResumeToken) IsExpired(now int64) bool { return now >= t.ExpiresAt }
```

docs-bot: snippet-harness/5950 succeeded (py,ts,go)

priya: LGTM from docs. small nit: the TS helper uses 500ms base jitter; maybe set 200ms so examples run faster when users try them locally.

aj: changed base to 200ms.

harry: thanks all. I'll merge after CI passes on the main pipeline. If anything else pops up ping me here.
